findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns "Clients" instead of client IDs and skips per-client permissions
findings.body:
`getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds each `resource.getName()` to the result.

The only resource with type `Clients` is the schema's all-clients resource, whose name is the literal string "Clients". Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` with no type set.

Consequences:
- Callers that expect a set of client IDs receive "Clients" when an all-clients permission is granted.
- Clients granted through individual per-client permissions are never returned.
- Any list filtering based on this method is wrong.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource cannot be resolved
findings.body:
When no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null in several cases: when the schema is not supported for the realm (admin permissions disabled), when the type is unknown, or when the resource is missing.

The result is passed straight to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` and then dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()` without a null check. A null here produces an NPE, and the admin request fails with a 500 instead of a simple deny.

The sibling `hasPermission(String)` does null-check its resource; this path should too.

findings.title: Client removal listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2
findings.body:
The listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1), but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled.

`ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. If both features are enabled, every `ClientRemovedEvent` triggers that exception, which can make client deletion fail.

The gate should either check that V2 is not active, or V2 should implement or no-op cleanup.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports in new class
findings.body:
`getEvaluationContext` is a private method that is never called. The `logger` field and the imports `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `Scope` and `Collections`-adjacent helpers are also unused.

`canExchangeTo` throws, so this token-exchange context code is leftover copy-paste. It should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: getResourceName not updated for Clients resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` only maps the Users type to a human-readable name: "All users" or the username.

For the newly added Clients type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. For per-client resources that is null or the internal UUID, so permissions on clients will display UUIDs rather than clientId or "All clients".

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says "Returns true"
findings.body:
The Javadoc for `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if ...", but both methods are void.

They actually throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails. The text should read like the other `require*` docs: "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false".

findings.title: Created roles not cleaned up and responses not closed
findings.body:
`testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles `myclient-role` and `myclient-subRole` with `roles().create(...)`. The returned Response is never closed, and no cleanup is registered via `realm.cleanup()`.

The roles leak into the shared managed realm, which can break re-runs or other tests that create roles with the same names (409 conflict).
